1 --- 2 title: Ensuring instant navigations 3 description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations. 4 nav_title: Instant navigation 5 related: 6 title: Learn more 7 description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation. 8 links: 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching 11 - app/getting-started/caching 12 - app/getting-started/revalidating 13 - app/guides/prefetching 14 --- 15 16 This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests. 17 18 ## What "instant" means 19 20 A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks. 21 22 > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns. 40 41 ## Quick start 42 43 Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear: 44 45 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 46 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 47 48 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 49 cacheComponents: true, 50 partialPrefetching: true, 51 } 52 53 export default nextConfig 54 ``` 55 56 To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption). If you'd like to enable everything, give your agent this prompt: 57 58 ```prompt 59 Adopt Cache Components and Partial Prefetching in this app so its navigations become instant. There is a Skill for each migration. 60 61 1. Before you change anything, explain to me in plain terms what Instant Navigation is and what adopting it will change. 62 63 2. Install the Skills you need, then verify your changes against a running dev server with next-dev-loop and agent-browser as you go: 64 - next-cache-components-adoption: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption 65 - next-partial-prefetching-adoption: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption 66 - next-dev-loop: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-dev-loop 67 68 3. Each Skill leaves decisions to me, like how much of the work lands in each pull request. Put those questions to me and wait for my answers instead of deciding on my behalf. Adopt Cache Components first, then Partial Prefetching, following the workflow each Skill lays out. Don't rush to a passing build. 69 70 4. When you finish a step, show me a table of the routes you touched and what changed on each, and talk me through what it means for the app. Keep it to the outcome, not the implementation details. 71 ``` 72 73 The rest of this guide covers the tools these migrations use, walks a navigation that blocks to instant, inspects what lands in the initial UI, and locks the result in with end-to-end tests. 74 75 ## The tools 76 77 ### Build the static shell 78 79 With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell. 80 81 > **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching. 82 83 **``** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves. 84 85 > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback. 86 87 Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data. 88 89 ### Prefetch URL data for a link 90 91 Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link. 92 93 To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch): 94 95 ```tsx 96 97 Checkout 98 99 ``` 100 101 With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click. 102 103 ### Validate instant navigation 104 105 By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached. 106 107 To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`: 108 109 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7} 110 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 111 112 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 113 cacheComponents: true, 114 experimental: { 115 instantInsights: { 116 validationLevel: 'manual-warning', 117 }, 118 }, 119 } 120 121 export default nextConfig 122 ``` 123 124
125 How validation simulates different navigations 126 127 For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 128 129 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 130 131 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 132 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 133 134 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 135 136
137 138 ### Test it in CI 139 140 The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern. 141 142 ### Inspect loading states 143 144 The **Navigation Inspector** in the Next.js DevTools freezes the page at its initial loading state, showing the static shell on direct visits and the prefetched destination on client navigations. Use the inspector to see how much meaningful content lands in the shell. 145 146 Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. See [Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) for the workflow. 147 148 See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell) for patterns to reduce fallback coverage and pull more content into the shell. 149 150 ## A page that navigates instantly 151 152 To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship. 313 314 The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. Other dynamic content remains blocked until the callback finishes. 371 372 > **Good to know:** The start of the `instant()` scope is the same as turning on **Pause on navigations** in the Navigation Inspector, and the end of the scope releases the pause the way **Resume** does. 373 374 For client navigations, wait for the destination URL before asserting on its UI. If the prefetched destination cannot commit, the URL wait times out and the test fails. 375 376 Run these against `next dev`, where the testing API is enabled automatically. To run them in CI against a production build, set `exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild` so `next start` exposes the same API: 377 378 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} 379 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 380 381 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 382 cacheComponents: true, 383 experimental: { exposeTestingApiInProductionBuild: true }, 384 } 385 386 export default nextConfig 387 ``` 388 389 Focus these tests on the user flows that matter most. 390 391 ## Fixing a navigation that blocks 392 393 Consider a different route, `/products/[slug]`, that fetches product data from a public API and shows a featured list alongside: 394 395 ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" 396 export default async function ProductPage( 397 props: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'> 398 ) { 399 const featured = await getFeatured() 400 const { slug } = await props.params 401 const res = await fetch(`https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products/${slug}`) 402 const product = await res.json() 403 404 return ( 405

498 499 Add a `"use cache"` directive to the fetching function: 500 501 ```tsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.tsx" 502 async function getFeatured() { 503 'use cache' 504 const res = await fetch('https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/products?limit=3') 505 return res.json() 506 } 507 ``` 508 509 The result is cached at the fetch level. The featured list ships with the App Shell. 510 511 > **Good to know:** In serverless deployments, in-memory caching with `"use cache"` will not persist across instances. Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. 512 513 Validation passes. Open the DevTools and try a client navigation. The featured section appears immediately, and **"Loading product..."** shows where the product details will stream in. 514 515 ### Iterate on loading states 516 517 {/* TODO: diagram — before/after illustration showing a single high-up Suspense boundary being refined down to smaller boundaries closer to the data */} 518 519 Validation passing means the navigation is instant. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation. 520 521 The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. A product page that keeps the header, image, and description visible with only the price and availability behind a fallback feels faster than a full-page skeleton, even at the same total load time. 522 523 Use the [DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) to see what your users see, or see the [AI workflow](#ai-workflow) for automating the loop with an agent. 524 525 ## AI workflow 526 527 At a high level, an agent optimizes a single navigation like this: 528 529 - **Observe**: read validation insights and choose the exact navigation and UI that should appear immediately. 530 - **Test**: confirm the target UI renders normally, then write an `instant()` test and verify that it fails before changing the route. 531 - **Fix**: validation errors name a specific component and suggest a fix (`use cache` or ``). The agent applies the fix and re-runs validation. 532 - **Verify**: run the test against a production-like build and keep the passing test as a regression guard. 533 534 The agent doesn't need to understand the full caching model, only to follow the insights and errors until they're gone. It does need your app-specific intent, though. Tell it what should appear immediately, what can stream in, and what must stay fresh. When a caching decision is unclear, keep the data fresh behind `` rather than guessing a cache lifetime. 535 536 For [iterating on loading states](#iterate-on-loading-states), a prompt like "maximize my content, and reduce the amount that needs to be behind a spinner" works well for pushing boundaries down. 537 538 Agents working on a Cache Components route typically reach for three levers: 539 540 - **Push down**: extract I/O into a Suspense-wrapped child so the parent stays static and static siblings lift into the shell. 541 - **Cache**: pair `'use cache'` with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) to assign a freshness profile. 542 - **Per-link prefetching** (nav-only): when a route reads URL data (`searchParams` or `params`), opt it into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) so the framework resolves that data at link-prefetch time. Session data from `cookies()` or `headers()` already lands in the App Shell without it. 543 544 Each refactor should pair with a before/after capture to verify the change actually landed. Identical-looking captures mean the refactor didn't take effect. 545 546 For agents to see what their changes actually render, pair this with [agent-browser](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser). With React DevTools enabled it reports the component tree and which `` boundaries are still pending, so an agent can make a change, snapshot the shell, check what landed, and adjust. See [Runtime visibility](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility) in the AI agents guide for the setup. 547 548 The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents#next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill packages this loop. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both. 549 550 ## Opting out 551 552 Not every layout or page can or should be instant. When the structural fix isn't worth the work, or when a route isn't a priority for instant navigation, refine validation at one of two scopes. 553 554 The dev overlay surfaces this as the **Block** fix alongside every insight: 555 556 557 566 567 568 Set `instant = false` on the page or layout file. 1 --- 2 title: Ensuring instant navigations 3 description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations. 4 nav_title: Instant navigation 5 related: 6 title: Learn more 7 description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation. 8 links: 9 - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant 10 - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching 11 - app/getting-started/caching 12 - app/getting-started/revalidating 13 - app/guides/prefetching 14 --- 15 16 This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests. 17 18 ## What "instant" means 19 20 A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks. 21 22 > **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait. 23 24 A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition. 25 26 Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout. 27 28
29 Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI 30 31 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. 32 33 On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. 34 35 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load. 36 37
38 39 With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns. 40 41 ## Quick start 42 43 Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear: 44 45 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 46 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 47 48 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 49 cacheComponents: true, 50 partialPrefetching: true, 51 } 52 53 export default nextConfig 54 ``` 55 56 To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption). If you'd like to enable everything, give your agent this prompt: 57 58 ```prompt 59 Adopt Cache Components and Partial Prefetching in this app so its navigations become instant. There is a Skill for each migration. 60 61 1. Before you change anything, explain to me in plain terms what Instant Navigation is and what adopting it will change. 62 63 2. Install the Skills you need, then verify your changes against a running dev server with next-dev-loop and agent-browser as you go: 64 - next-cache-components-adoption: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption 65 - next-partial-prefetching-adoption: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption 66 - next-dev-loop: https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-dev-loop 67 68 3. Each Skill leaves decisions to me, like how much of the work lands in each pull request. Put those questions to me and wait for my answers instead of deciding on my behalf. Adopt Cache Components first, then Partial Prefetching, following the workflow each Skill lays out. Don't rush to a passing build. 69 70 4. When you finish a step, show me a table of the routes you touched and what changed on each, and talk me through what it means for the app. Keep it to the outcome, not the implementation details. 71 ``` 72 73 The rest of this guide covers the tools these migrations use, walks a navigation that blocks to instant, inspects what lands in the initial UI, and locks the result in with end-to-end tests. 74 75 ## The tools 76 77 ### Build the static shell 78 79 With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell. 80 81 > **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching. 82 83 **``** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves. 84 85 > **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback. 86 87 Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. Partial Prefetching uses the App Shell as the default `` prefetch. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached content that depends on that link's URL data. 88 89 ### Prefetch URL data for a link 90 91 Under [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), each visible `` prefetches the destination's App Shell by default. Links to the same route share one App Shell instead of triggering a separate App Shell request for each link. 92 93 To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch): 94 95 ```tsx 96 97 Checkout 98 99 ``` 100 101 With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click. 102 103 ### Validate instant navigation 104 105 By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached. 106 107 To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`: 108 109 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7} 110 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 111 112 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 113 cacheComponents: true, 114 experimental: { 115 instantInsights: { 116 validationLevel: 'manual-warning', 117 }, 118 }, 119 } 120 121 export default nextConfig 122 ``` 123 124
125 How validation simulates different navigations 126 127 For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 128 129 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 130 131 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 132 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 133 134 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 135 136
137 138 ### Test it in CI 139 140 The `@next/playwright` package provides an [`instant()`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#testing-instant-navigation) helper that scopes your assertions to the UI that's immediately available on navigation, so regressions surface in CI. See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern. 141 142 ### Inspect loading states 143 144 The **Navigation Inspector** in the Next.js DevTools freezes the page at its initial loading state, showing the static shell on direct visits and the prefetched destination on client navigations. Use the inspector to see how much meaningful content lands in the shell. 145 146 Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. See [Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) for the workflow. 147 148 See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell) for patterns to reduce fallback coverage and pull more content into the shell. 149 150 ## A page that navigates instantly 151 152 To see the primitives in action, consider a small store app. Each product has its own page at `/store/[slug]`, reachable from the homepage and from other product pages. The panel shows **Awaiting navigation...** With the toggle on, the next refresh or link click freezes the page so you can inspect the shell. 259 260 Refresh the product page. The Inspector freezes and shows **Loading shell** labeled **Page load** with the target URL. In the app, two fallbacks appear: "Loading product..." and "Checking availability...". Each navigation pauses as long as the toggle is on. 307 308 > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. Client-side hooks like `useSearchParams` suspend on page loads (search params are not known at build time) but resolve synchronously on client navigations (the router already has the params). 309 310 ## Prevent regressions with e2e tests 311 312 Validation catches structural problems during development, but as the codebase grows, the structural checks can only tell you that a shell exists. They can't tell you whether the right content is in it. E2E tests close that gap: they assert on what the user actually sees when the navigation completes, catching regressions before they ship. 313 314 The [`@next/playwright`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@next/playwright) package includes an `instant()` helper for this. It does not mean the loading states are good. A `` boundary placed high in the tree (say, wrapping the whole page) might satisfy validation, but it replaces most of the page with a single fallback on every navigation. 520 521 The best loading states keep as much real, cached content visible as possible and only show fallbacks where data is actually in flight. It confirms the target UI renders normally, writes an `instant()` test that fails before the fix, then works it to green against a production-like build and ships it as a regression guard. Use it for the initial load (hard navigation), client-side navigation (soft navigation), or both. 549 550 ## Opting out 551 552 Not every layout or page can or should be instant. events.content:
Fixed. The product page title now renders instantly; only the stock count and price stream in afterward. **What was wrong** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component, and `getInventory` calls `connection()` (plus `Math.random()`), which forces request-time rendering. Because that await sat above everything in the page, the entire route — including the static "Premium Widget" heading — had to wait for the server on every navigation. With `cacheComponents: true`, this also meant the route had no static shell to prefetch. **The change** (`app/product/page.tsx`) I moved the inventory read into a separate async `Inventory` component and wrapped it in `Checking availability...

}>`. The page component itself is now synchronous, so the `

` is part of the prerendered shell that the home page's `` prefetches and shows immediately on click. Inventory stays uncached (it's meant to be fresh per request), so it streams into the fallback once `connection()` resolves. This is the exact "push down into Suspense" pattern the bundled Next.js docs recommend for Cache Components. **Verification** `next build` succeeds and the route table now shows `/product` as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content — where before it would have been fully dynamic. Type-checking passes too. One note: `next build` automatically rewrote `tsconfig.json` (setting `jsx` to `react-jsx` and adding `.next/dev/types` to `include`) and generated `.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`. I reverted the tsconfig and removed those artifacts so the diff only contains the fix, but Next.js will reapply the tsconfig changes the next time you run `dev` or `build`, and you may want to add `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` to `.gitignore`.
